text:
Charlie McAvoy has played 12 of Boston's 18 games, and in them the Bruins have looked like a different team. They get 61% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, more than ten points better than without him. For a defenseman playing 24 minutes a night against top lines, that's the number that matters most.

The scoresheet is quieter. One goal and 9 points, all 8 of his points in the last ten games coming as assists, including a four-assist night against Nashville. His shooting is low (4.8%) against a usual range near 7%, so a few more goals are owed.

The assists come with a caveat: Boston has scored 6.5 more goals than expected with him on, which pads them. Evolving-Hockey had him 30th of 215 defensemen last season, driving play at the 88th percentile against 95th-percentile competition, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a defenseman who gets to the home-plate area more than most. He also started a brawl with Vegas this month, per Markerzone. Watch the five-on-five share: that's his real line.
headline: McAvoy is driving play, if not scoring
